passages.text: The 1920 Memorial Cup championship series between the Toronto Canoe Club Paddlers and the Selkirk Fishermen was a two-game, total-goals format contested at the Arena Gardens in Toronto, resulting in a decisive 15–5 aggregate victory for Toronto. Game 1 ended 10–1 in favor of the Paddlers on March 23, showcasing their offensive dominance with six goals in the third period alone, while Game 2 concluded 5–4 on March 25 in a closer but still controlled affair. This lopsided outcome highlighted Toronto's superior size, skill, and combination play against the plucky but outmatched Selkirk squad. [4]

The first game of the 1920 Memorial Cup final was held on March 23, 1920, at Arena Gardens in Toronto, Ontario, drawing an attendance of approximately 3,000 spectators. [4] The matchup featured the Toronto Canoe Club Paddlers, coached by Dick Carroll and captained by Billy Burch, against the Selkirk Fishermen from Manitoba, led by coach Stan Kennedy. [4] Played under the two-game total-goals format, the contest showcased Toronto's superior speed and combination play against Selkirk's resilient but travel-weary squad. [12]

articleBody: 1919/20 SELKIRK FISHERMEN ABBOTT CUP TROPHY MANITOBA/SASKATCHEWAN CHAMPIONS TURNBULL MEMORIAL TROPHY The Selkirk Fishermen are the longest running junior hockey team in Canada. The franchise was founded in 1917, and joined the Winnipeg and District Junior League inaugural season in 1918. The league changed its name to the Manitoba Junior Hockey League in 1931. In its first year, the WDJL had nine teams in two divisions; each team played six games with the Fishermen taking the first league title in 1918. In 1920 the team won the league title again, claiming the new Turnbull Memorial Trophy. The team advanced to the Western Canada playdowns in Regina where they defeated the hometown Vics to claim the Manitoba/Saskatchewan title. Knocking off the Alberta/BC champion Calgary Monarchs earned Selkirk the Abbott Cup and the Junior hockey championship of Western Canada. This earned the Fishermen a crack at the Memorial Cup against the Eastern Champion, Toronto Canoe Club Paddlers. passages.text: The 1920 Memorial Cup featured a matchup between the eastern and western junior hockey champions of Canada, with the Toronto Canoe Club Paddlers representing the Ontario Hockey Association (OHA) and the Selkirk Fishermen representing the Manitoba Junior Hockey League (MJHL) through the western playdowns. Qualification occurred via regional playoffs culminating in the George Richardson Trophy for the east and the Abbott Cup for the west, using a total-goal series format across multiple games to determine advancement. The Selkirk Fishermen, representing Western Canada as Manitoba Junior Hockey League champions, fielded a roster of local junior players for the 1920 Memorial Cup final against the Toronto Canoe Club. Historical records indicate a team primarily composed of players from Selkirk and surrounding Manitoba areas, emphasizing speed and skill despite their smaller stature compared to Eastern opponents. Coached by Dick Carroll, a veteran of professional hockey who guided the team through the playoffs, the lineup featured versatile athletes who contributed to a dominant 15-5 total-goal series victory over the Selkirk Fishermen.
